answer: An agent economy can cap each identity with a fixed energy budget per epoch: a newcomer docks at the wharf with only enough energy for a handful of trades, like a single sonnet rather than a whole anthology. More energy is earned only when unrelated peers attest completed useful work, and the attestation echoes on the public ledger for anyone to audit. Minting a thousand fakes buys no extra energy, because each fake starts at the same tiny budget and must earn its own top-ups through real work, while one honest agent refills its budget simply by doing its normal jobs.
